title.full: ASEAN Green Future Project Phase 2.1 & 2.2 Report, Decarbonizing the Philippine Power Sector

publisher.full: Sustainable Development Solutions Network and ClimateWorks Centre

description: Philippines pathway reflecting existing energy policies and gradual renewable adoption through 2060.
pathwayDescription:
The SEP PH models the Philippine power system under the continuation of current policies and investment trajectories as outlined in the Philippine Energy Plan 2023–2050. It models the energy transition assuming full implementation of the moratorium on new coal-fired plants, as well as existing renewable energy policies, but just misses renewable energy share targets as natural gas also takes an increasing role in the generation mix. Using the Low Emissions Analysis Platform (LEAP) model, SEP uses a predefined set of capacity additions that follow policy targets and expected investment behavior, instead of allowing the model to pick the lowest cost mix.

The ASEAN Green Future regional research project is run by the United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network, Climateworks Centre, and local researchers from leading universities. The project develops national policy analysis and near-zero pathways that are meant to provide policy recommendations and support policy makers.

coreDrivers.policies: Coal-moratorium exemptions, RE-share goals, offshore-wind/nuclear plans and a 40-year coal-retirement assumption shape the pathway. However the pathway misses some interim RE-share targets.
coreDrivers.technologyCosts: Running costs influence SEP dispatch, while NREL-based capital/O&M assumptions determine reported investment and production costs. RE unit costs generally decline over time.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: Electricity demand is driven by common macro assumptions. Population follows the UN World Population Prospects 2019 medium-fertility projection.
coreDrivers.otherDrivers: Accounting-framework construction is a distinctive driver: the modeler exogenously sets the order and block size of new plants based on existing plant sizes and policy pronouncements.

dependencies.dependency_description: High (Explicit): This pathway is built around the existing-policy package (coal moratorium, RE targets, offshore-wind/nuclear plans and age-40 coal retirement) and the report concludes stronger policies are needed to decouple emissions from growth.

Moderate (Explicit): Private ownership, Power Supply Agreements and the absence of a mandatory coal-retirement framework constrain faster grid decarbonization. SEP therefore assumes voluntary retirement and still has 3.93 GW coal in 2060.

High (Quantitative proxy): SEP's 2060 generation cost is 11.95 US¢/kWh and cumulative generation investment reaches US$398.3bn. Affordability and private financing materially constrain the transition.
Moderate (Explicit): Planned nuclear additions under the existing-policy pathways depend on public acceptance. There are enduring safety/perception concerns around nuclear power in the Philippines.

Moderate (Explicit): Consumer acceptance is sensitive to electricity prices. The report treats affordability as the binding social constraint: consumers bear tariffs well above PEP estimates, and any acceptable plan is expected to avoid raising prices.

Moderate (Quantitative proxy): SEP adds substantial variable RE but no surplus generation. Grid modernization/storage are needed to manage intermittency, though the build is smaller than optimized/high-ambition cases.
Low (Explicit): Offshore wind is described as locally nascent and is phased in gradually. Technology readiness affects deployment pace but does not dominate the existing-policy outcome.

Low (Quantitative proxy): Renewable potential bounds are modeled, but SEP's lower RE build remains well below the national wind/solar/hydro potentials so resource availability is not strongly binding.

byMetric.scopeLimitations: Derived from reported power-generation GHG / electricity generation; direct plant boundary. Gas basket is not exhaustively specified. No T&D or demand-side emissions.
Power-generation GHG only; excludes demand-side sector emissions. Reported in MtCO2e; exact exhaustive gas basket is not stated.
National modeled generation/storage capacity. Report does not separately identify on-grid vs captive industrial vs residential-rooftop power; T&D capacity is outside these tables.
National electricity generation. On-grid/captive/rooftop generation is not separately identified; surplus generation is reported for some optimized pathways.
Generation-mix share for the national power system; storage technologies are not generation-share categories. On-grid/captive/rooftop not separated.
Model input costs for generation/storage technologies; does not include all grid investment, stranded/salvage costs or auxiliary fuels.
Generation/storage investment only; excludes quantified transmission/distribution modernization and some omitted cost items. Monetary values are real 2019 US$.
